archetype.name: Lottery Team (no rim protection)
archetype.definition: A team whose defense cannot stop anything near the basket and whose offense lacks the shooting to cover for it, so it is losing by margins that put it at the very bottom of the league.

report.headline: Not unlucky, just overrun: the rim defense has collapsed and nothing covers it
report.take:
Sacramento is 0-6, last on the site's Teams tab, and the record is an honest reflection of its play. The Net Rtg of -18.4 ranks 30th, the point differential implies one win rather than zero, and the closest loss was 120-128 to Portland. This is not a team losing close games and waiting for a bounce. It is getting beaten on both ends by large margins, with an offensive rating of 105.6 and a defensive rating of 124, both 29th.

The defense is the core problem. Opponents post a 60.3 eFG %, worst in the league, and shoot 75.5% at the rim, which is 10.2 points above the league average and also last. The telling detail is that the Opp Rim Rate is roughly league-average: Sacramento is not allowing an unusual number of rim attempts, it simply cannot contest the ones it allows. This did not come out of nowhere. Last season's defense ranked 28th with a 121.5 DRtg and a 69.8 Opp Rim FG %, and the defense has finished in the bottom third in four of the last five years. What happened this season is that a long-running weakness got worse. The position splits point the same way: small forwards are scoring well above their usual output against this team (the worst in the league on that measure), and power forwards are close behind.

The offense cannot outscore that. Sacramento takes few threes (38 3PA Rate, 27th) and makes few (30.4%), and it does not create second chances (22.9 ORB %, 28th). Darius Acuff Jr. runs the most possessions at a 33.2 USG % on a 50.4 TS %, which is a lot of offense flowing through inefficient shots. The efficient options are underused. Domantas Sabonis is shooting a 74.9 TS % with a 4.1 BPM and ranks 8th of 79 on his tab. Zach LaVine is at 62.9 and De'Andre Hunter at 61.4. Sabonis is the main reason the frontcourt grades C+ while the backcourt sits at D-. The on-off numbers are scrambled over six games, with LaVine at -24.3 and Acuff at +18.3, so treat them as noise rather than a verdict on either player.

Some improvement is coming, because a 75% conversion rate at the rim allowed is extreme even for a bad defense, and last year's team was roughly a -10 Net Rtg club. Improving from historically awful to merely bad still leaves Sacramento in the lottery, though. The last five games were only slightly less lopsided than the season as a whole, and the most recent was a 31-point loss in Memphis.

strengths.title: Sabonis as an efficient hub
strengths.body: Sabonis is the one clearly above-average piece: 96 points on a 74.9 TS %, 95 rebounds and 44 assists, a 4.1 BPM, and the 8th spot of 79 on his tab. That production comes from finishing inside and creating for others rather than from shooting volume, which is why his usage is only 16.1%. That TS % will come down over a full season, but he is the reason the frontcourt grade is passable, and the offense would likely improve if more possessions ran through him.

strengths.title: Defensive glass still holds
strengths.body: The one part of the defense that works is ending possessions after a miss. The 73.8 DRB % ranks 11th and sits above the league average. Opponents are not beating Sacramento with second chances. They are scoring on their first shot. That points the fix at contesting shots rather than at effort on the boards, and it is consistent with last season's 73.5.

strengths.title: Efficient secondary scorers
strengths.body: LaVine (62.9 TS %) and Hunter (61.4 TS %) are converting their shots well, even though the team as a whole sits 25th in TS %. The problem is distribution more than talent, since the highest-usage player is the least efficient of the main scorers. LaVine is listed day-to-day, which matters given how few efficient creators this roster has.

concerns.title: Rim defense has collapsed
concerns.body: Opponents finish 75.5% at the rim, last in the league and 10.2 points above average, and that drives an Opp eFG % of 60.3, also last. The volume of rim attempts allowed is normal, so the failure is in contesting shots, not in keeping opponents out of the paint. The current rate is likely to come down somewhat, but last year's 69.8 shows the underlying level is still poor.

concerns.title: Low-volume, low-accuracy offense
concerns.body: Sacramento shoots too few threes (38 3PA Rate, 27th) and makes too few of them (30.4%, 4.3 points below the league average). It also rarely grabs its own misses, with a 22.9 ORB %. With Acuff using a third of possessions on a 50.4 TS %, the result is a 105.6 ORtg, 29th. The three-point percentage should rise somewhat, but the low attempt rate is a choice about shot profile, not bad luck.

concerns.title: Forwards getting torched
concerns.body: Small forwards are scoring 9.25 points above their own averages against Sacramento, the worst figure in the league, and power forwards 4.06 above, which ranks 29th. The wings grade is D+, and Keegan Murray has played only two of six games, shooting a 37.3 TS % in them. The forward rotation has neither depth nor size, and nothing in the sheet suggests a fix.

trend.note: The last five games were marginally less lopsided than the season overall, at -17.8 per game, but every result has been a clear loss and the latest was the biggest. There is no turn yet.

weekAhead.headline: Three winning teams, then Miami: the best chance comes last
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at Dallas (4-2, 12th on the site), then brings three home games: the Lakers (5-2, 6th), San Antonio (4-2, 10th), and Miami (2-4, 19th). The Lakers have the league's best eFG % at 60.0 and the third-ranked offense, a bad matchup for a defense allowing the most efficient shooting in the league. San Antonio already beat Sacramento 130-103 and brings a 7th-ranked defense with a strong interior.

Miami is the realistic chance. Its defense ranks 24th, it allows 40.5% from three (29th), and opposing shooting guards score heavily against it, which suits LaVine if he plays. The catch is that Miami protects the rim well, and Sabonis's game depends on interior finishing. Sacramento probably needs a hot shooting night to get its first win.

keyMatchups.title: Sabonis vs Dallas's center defense
keyMatchups.body: Dallas holds centers to 14.33 points, 3rd-fewest in the league and well under their own averages, while power forwards score heavily against it. That suggests Sacramento should get its offense from the power forward spot rather than through Sabonis in the post. Given how little the Kings' power forwards have produced, that is a tough ask.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances against the Lakers
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers rank 29th in DRB % at 67.2, the clearest weakness they have. Sacramento's own ORB % is just 22.9, but Sabonis on the glass is the one way to turn that weakness into extra possessions against a team that shoots far better. Opposing point guards also score 40 points a game against the Lakers, so Acuff's high usage could pay off here if his shots fall.

keyMatchups.title: Miami's leaky perimeter defense
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows 40.5% from three, 29th in the league, and 35.83 points to shooting guards, 26th. That is the matchup for LaVine and for a three-point attack that has been cold. Miami's rim defense ranks 3rd, so the Kings have to win this one from outside.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the Opp Rim FG % starts falling from 75.5. Until it does, no matchup this week is winnable without a hot shooting night.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect improvement but not respectability. A -18.4 Net Rtg is an extreme figure. The rim defense and three-point shooting should both move back toward this franchise's recent levels, and last year's team was roughly a -10 club that won 22 games. The parts that look structural are a defense that has ranked near the bottom for years, a shot profile light on threes, and a forward group without depth. None of those changes on its own over the remaining 76 games. A finish somewhere around 18 to 25 wins, with a Net Rtg near -9 to -12, fits a team that stops getting blown out every night but still loses most of its games.

The main upside lever is redistributing the offense toward Sabonis, LaVine and Hunter, the three efficient scorers, and away from low-percentage, high-usage creation. Whether that happens, and whether Murray returns to a regular role, decides whether this is a bottom-three team or merely a lottery team.
swingFactors: Rim defense moving back toward last year's level
Shot distribution away from Acuff's high-usage, low-efficiency volume

confidence.note: Only six games, but the margins are large and consistent and the defensive problems echo past seasons.
